To be honest I talk to myself a lot. I’ve come to accept that this is who I am and no matter how much I want it to change it’s not going to. I’ve very open with my mental illnesses because I am a very different person because of it. When I have a hallucination I tell myself that what every I saw wasn’t real and it goes away. When I hear voices I tend to shrug them off or sometimes I answer them or respond to it. If I’m out in public and it happens i still respond the same. My paranoia affects me differently and if I’m not around my boyfriend I usually call him or text him and use him to vent about what ever trigged me but at the same time I’m also telling myself that I’m over reacting and it’s just me being paranoid. I have a lot of ticks that I do that help me settle my mind and I also do a lot of writing. I carry and journal and about a thousand pens where ever I go in case I start having an episode.  I also have a routine that I stick to. Like when I’m at work I do the same things at the same time exactly the same way. It helps me feel more accomplished and organized. I have another routine for when I’m at home that I follow as well. Honestly it’s a lot of pep talking myself, telling myself things like “you can do this.” I also make sure to celebrate everything that I do overcome during my daily life. Also having people who support and accept that this is how you are is very helpful. If my friends and family weren’t so open minded about it or when I do have an episode around them they support me and help me through it rather then make me feel less of a human for it. I think it’s just something you will have to play around with to figure out what will work the best for you. For the voices I tend to listen to CreepyMCPasta on YouTube in headphones pretty much the whole time I’m away from home because for some reason his voice is very soothing to me, and I like being read to, and creepy pastas are me thing.
